family.amstrad-series-8.description: The 1992 professional offering developed with Intel, split into ISA-based ES and EISA-based LP lines.
family.amstrad-series-8.history: In June 1992, Tilt presented the 8000 range as the professional successor to the 3000 generation under an Amstrad–Intel agreement. SVM tested the LP8486 in September and positioned ES8486 as the lower-cost alternative. Amstrad supplied its specifications; SVM attributes Irish manufacture of the LP system unit, excluding monitor and keyboard, to Intel. Integration was the main distinction: LP combined EISA, SCSI and Ethernet, while ES retained ISA. British advertising in January 1993 documents both lines on sale.
